You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository fastapi/fastapi.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix evaluating stringified annotations in Python 3.10

I've bumped into the exact same issue as https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/discussions/598 so I solved it like https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/pull/721  :smile: 

I'll try to add tests soon but if you can do it faster, please feel free !!

## Task Budget (Session terminates when any budget is exhausted)
- Time allowance: 4.5 minutes
- Tool calls allowance: 80 calls
- Max loop iterations: 160 turns

## Execution Environment Rules
- Single command timeout: 180 seconds (commands exceeding this fail without ending the session)
- Command output limit: 5000 characters
- File view limit: 150 lines per read_file call
- File character limit: 10000 characters per read_file call
- Environment is offline (no network/PyPI access). All repository and test dependencies are ALREADY pre-installed. Do NOT attempt to run pip install or download packages.

0. All source code is under `/workspace`. Do NOT search outside `/workspace` (e.g. `/usr/`, `/wheels/`, system site-packages). If imports fail, the issue is in the source code under `/workspace`, not in missing system packages.
1. Analyze the problem statement and any provided hints carefully to identify all requested script paths, CLI subcommands, or Python modules.
2. Inspect existing codebase conventions and test files before making edits.
3. Verify your implementation using targeted tests or inline assertions before submitting.
4. Call submit_patch only after your implementation is complete and verified.
5. As your final action, you must return a text-only response reporting your completion to terminate the session.
## Code Intelligence Tools
This repository has pre-built code graph and embedding data. Use these tools for fast, targeted navigation:
- `search_similar_code(query)`: Find semantically similar functions/classes by keyword.
- `get_code_neighbors(node)`: Find callers, callees, and definitions related to a symbol.
- `get_code_subgraph(nodes)`: Get the induced subgraph for a set of symbols.

{"skill_name": "code-map", "instructions": "# code-map

Run with `run_skill_script(skill_name="code-map", file_path="scripts/code_map.py", args=[COMMAND, NAME])`.
`args` is a list of strings.

| Command | args example | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| find | `["find", "solve_dependencies"]` | qualified node name, `file:start-end`, signature |
| callers | `["callers", "solve_dependencies"]` | every call site: `file:line`, enclosing function, source line |
| callees | `["callees", "solve_dependencies"]` | names called inside that function |
| outline | `["outline", "fastapi/routing.py"]` | classes/functions of one file with line ranges |

- Add `"--tests"` to include test files; add `"--limit", "50"` for more rows.
- NAME can be bare (`get_dependant`), `Class.method`, or a dotted path.
- The qualified name printed by `find` (e.g. `fastapi.dependencies.utils.solve_dependencies`) is the exact `node` to pass to `get_code_neighbors` and `search_similar_code`.", "frontmatter": {"name": "code-map", "description": "Structural code lookup with Python ast. FILE: fastapi/params.py
LINES: 100-110
FUNCTION: get_type_hints
ROOT_CAUSE: In Python 3.10, stringified annotations (from `from __future__ import annotations`) are not automatically evaluated by `typing.get_type_hints` if the module is not available in the global namespace or if the types are defined in a way that requires explicit evaluation.
PROPOSED_CHANGE: Update the call to `get_type_hints` to include `globalns` and `localns` to ensure stringified annotations are correctly resolved.
OTHER_LOCATIONS: none
TEST_FILE: none found
CONFIDENCE: medium
